profile.title: AI & Data Engineer
profile.intro: As a Data & AI Engineer with a degree from ESILV, I transform raw industrial data (CATIA 3D models, telecom network data) into AI models that automate tasks that were previously performed manually. From graph neural networks (GNNs) to multi-agent architectures, I have led these projects at Dassault Systèmes and SFR.
profile.vision: My goal: to combine robust data engineering with generative AI to deliver tools that save engineers time—without replacing them—particularly in 3D and industrial automation.

education.description: Specialization in Deep Learning, NLP, Big Data and MLOps.
Mathematics, physics, chemistry and computer science preparation for engineering school.

experience.description:
• 3D Machine Learning (GNN): Improvement and extension to new vehicles of a GNN model that recognizes parts in a CATIA model to automate 3D measurements. Faster and more robust pipeline for previously unseen vehicles.

• CAD Data Engineering: Redesign of geometric feature extraction using CATIA Visual Scripting. Lighter data and a more accurate model.

• Agent-Based AI: Development of a multi-agent orchestrator (Agent-to-Agent, MCP, LangGraph) for a proof of concept in regulatory verification for an industrial client.

• AI Agent Evaluation: Design of test scenarios, identification of limitations, and provision of structured feedback to development teams.

• Client Relations: Preparation of demonstrations and supporting materials for key accounts in the Transportation & Mobility sector.

• Anomaly detection from scratch: design of a complete pipeline (PCAP → graphs) and a GNN that identifies the type of anomaly from among 40 classes with approximately 81% accuracy.

• LLM-based localization: an unsupervised prototype that highlights suspicious areas of a call within a Flask web interface.

• MLOps: automated training via GitLab and Jenkins. Results were presented twice to management, which deemed the project worthy of future investment.

• RAG Chatbot: an on-premises assistant delivered in one week to answer questions about the Lab’s processes.

• Optimized the application's core AI algorithm.

• Improved reliability through unit and functional testing.

• Contributed to UX and architecture decisions during brainstorming sessions.
Tutoring middle school and high school students in mathematics.

projects.title: Detection of Network Anomalies in PCAP Files
projects.shortDescription: Classification of anomaly types (GNN) and error localization (unsupervised LLM) in call recordings. SFR internship project, built from scratch.
projects.description: Internship at SFR (Vélizy Lab, April–August 2025). Starting from scratch, I built a complete pipeline: PCAP → JSON (Tshark) → graphs, sequences, or vectors, and then compared GNNs, RNNs, and DNNs. The GNN classifies 40 classes of SIP anomalies with approximately 81% accuracy. A second tool, still in the prototype stage, locates errors using a language model trained on normal calls and displays them in a Flask web interface.
features: Comparison of GNNs, RNNs, DNNs, and Autoencoders

projects.title: SFR Lab's Internal RAG Chatbot
projects.shortDescription: A local assistant that answers questions about the Lab's processes and terminology, developed in just a few days toward the end of an internship at SFR.
projects.description: I built this during the last week of my internship at SFR. The chatbot searches for relevant passages in a local database, supplements the context using web scraping, and generates a response using an LLM via LangChain and Hugging Face—all entirely on-premises. It answers questions about Lab processes, business definitions, and practical issues; the ability to read PCAP files still needed to be developed.
